question.problem:
Consider the function $y=\sqrt{({x}^{2}+1)^{3}(x-3)^{8}}.$ The derivative of this function is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}(x-3)^{3}(a{x}^{2}+bx+c).
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$
question.worked_solution:
Our function can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{({x}^{2}+1)^{3}(x-3)^{8}} \\  & =\sqrt{({x}^{2}+1)^{3}}\cdot \sqrt{(x-3)^{8}} \\  & =({x}^{2}+1)^{3/2}(x-3)^{8/2} \\  & =({x}^{2}+1)^{3/2}(x-3)^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the product and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+1)^{3/2}(x-3)^{4}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+1)^{3/2})+\operatorname{ln}⁡((x-3)^{4}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\cdot 2x+4\cdot \frac{1}{x-3} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{3x}{{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{4}{x-3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{3x}{{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{4}{x-3})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\sqrt{({x}^{2}+1)^{3}(x-3)^{8}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\sqrt{({x}^{2}+1)^{3}(x-3)^{8}}(\frac{3x}{{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{4}{x-3}) \\  & =\sqrt{({x}^{2}+1)^{3}(x-3)^{8}}(\frac{3x(x-3)+4({x}^{2}+1)}{({x}^{2}+1)(x-3)}) \\  & =\sqrt{({x}^{2}+1)^{3}(x-3)^{8}}(\frac{7{x}^{2}-9x+4}{({x}^{2}+1)(x-3)}) \\  & =({x}^{2}+1)^{3/2}(x-3)^{4}(\frac{7{x}^{2}-9x+4}{({x}^{2}+1)(x-3)}) \\  & =({x}^{2}+1)^{1/2}(x-3)^{3}(7{x}^{2}-9x+4) \\  & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}(x-3)^{3}(7{x}^{2}-9x+4)\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore,

$$
a+b+c=7+(-9)+4=2.
$$
